name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
summary: A row done lying chest-down on an incline bench, which removes lower-back and momentum demands so the upper back does the work.
setup: Set an adjustable bench to about 30-45 degrees.
Lie chest-down with your chest and head against the pad and feet planted on the floor.
Take a dumbbell in each hand and let the arms hang straight with the shoulders set.
execution: Row both dumbbells toward your hips, leading with the elbows.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower under control until the arms are straight.
Keep the chest on the pad throughout.
cues: Chest stays glued to the pad
mistakes: Lifting the chest off the pad: lower the weight and stay supported.
Shrugging up: keep the shoulders down and away from the ears.
Pulling the elbows too high and wide: row at about 45 degrees to the torso for the back.
Dropping the weights: lower slowly through the full stretch.
